title: Have We Found Aliens? Scientists Say 'Not So Fast!'
summary:
Have you ever wondered if we've found aliens? In 2025, some scientists made big announcements. They said they found possible signs of life on a planet called K2-18b and on Mars. But what do most scientists think? A new survey asked hundreds of alien experts, called astrobiologists, what they really believe.

For K2-18b, only 6.6% of scientists agreed that we probably found alien life. That's like if 100 scientists, only about 7 said yes. Nearly two-thirds said no. For Mars, more scientists were hopeful, but still cautious. Only 15.1% said yes.

But here's the interesting part: scientists didn't just say "no" and stop. Many moved from "definitely no" to "maybe not." They became more open to the idea, even if they weren't ready to say "yes."

Why are scientists so careful? Because sometimes things that look like life can be made by nature without life. For example, on Mars, scientists found "leopard spots" that could be made by tiny microbes, but they could also be made by chemicals. It's like seeing a shape in the clouds—it might look like a dragon, but it's just water vapor.

This survey is important because it shows that science isn't always about saying "yes" or "no." Sometimes it's about saying "we're not sure yet." And that's okay! Scientists are still exploring, and maybe one day we'll find real aliens. But for now, they're keeping their minds open and their excitement in check.
why_it_matters: It is important to know that science doesn't have all the answers right away — saying 'we're not sure yet' is part of how scientists test big ideas like whether we are alone in the universe.

keywords.explanation: Scientists who study the possibility of life beyond Earth.
A set of questions asked to many people to learn what they think.
Careful and not willing to say yes until the evidence is stronger.
Tiny living things, so small that you usually need a microscope to see them.
Water in the form of a gas, like the mist you see when water boils.
A faraway planet that scientists have been searching for possible signs of life.

questions.question: What did some scientists announce in 2025?
options: That Earth was the only planet with water
That telescopes can see tiny aliens
They found possible signs of life on a planet called K2-18b and on Mars
That they had proof aliens built spaceships
questions.correct_answer: They found possible signs of life on a planet called K2-18b and on Mars

questions.question: Who took part in the new survey?
options: Astronauts on the International Space Station
Hundreds of alien experts, called astrobiologists
People who have seen UFOs
Students in science class
questions.correct_answer: Hundreds of alien experts, called astrobiologists

questions.question: According to the survey, what did scientists think about K2-18b?
options: The scientists had no opinion
Everyone agreed that aliens live there
15.1% said yes and no one said no
Only 6.6% agreed that we probably found alien life, and nearly two-thirds said no
questions.correct_answer: Only 6.6% agreed that we probably found alien life, and nearly two-thirds said no

questions.question: How did scientists respond to the Mars announcements?
options: They all said definitely yes immediately
They were more hopeful but still cautious; only 15.1% said yes
They found real aliens on Mars
They refused to study Mars
questions.correct_answer: They were more hopeful but still cautious; only 15.1% said yes

questions.question: What change happened in the survey?
options: Many moved from 'maybe not' to 'definitely yes'
Many moved from 'definitely no' to 'maybe not'
Many moved from 'yes' to 'no'
Nobody changed their mind
questions.correct_answer: Many moved from 'definitely no' to 'maybe not'

questions.question: Why can scientists not be sure about the leopard spots on Mars?
options: Leopards on Mars hid the spots
The spots could be made by tiny microbes, but they could also be made by chemicals
The spots disappeared before scientists could study them
The rover's camera was broken
questions.correct_answer: The spots could be made by tiny microbes, but they could also be made by chemicals

background_read: Astrobiologists are scientists who study whether life could exist beyond Earth.
K2-18b is a planet that orbits a different star far away from our solar system, while Mars is Earth's rocky neighbor in space.
Scientists use surveys to show how many experts agree or disagree, especially when exciting claims about space are still not proven.
Article_Structure: WHO: Hundreds of alien experts, called astrobiologists, were asked what they think.
WHAT: Most did not say yes to alien life: 6.6% said yes for K2-18b and 15.1% said yes for Mars.
WHERE: The possible signs of life are on K2-18b, a planet far away, and on Mars, a nearby planet.
WHY: Scientists stay cautious because things that look like life can also form through chemistry without any living thing involved.

perspectives.description: Recent announcements made them hopeful that we might be closer to finding alien life, and they point out that many scientists are becoming more open to the idea.
They worry that a clue like the Mars leopard spots could be just chemistry, so they want stronger proof before anyone announces aliens.
They see the survey as a good example of how real science works: experts can disagree, change their minds, and still say we need more information.
